title: Extractor silently discards most of multi-section documents
acceptance: A document whose content lives in sibling sections extracts all of them, not the single best-scoring one
gutenberg_frankenstein extracts substantially all 24 chapters rather than chapter 24 alone
mdn_fetch_api, python_docs_tutorial, w3c_html4_tables, wikipedia_readability and wikinews_story extract their full prose
Each of those six gains a frozen expectation, replacing its documented finding in Fixtures/README.md
mdn_img_element and wikipedia_epub, which already extract completely, do not regress
Furniture rejection is not weakened to achieve this: nav, footers and reference lists still stay out
notes: THE MOST SERIOUS DEFECT FOUND SO FAR. Measured: gutenberg_frankenstein is ~75,085 words in source and the extractor keeps 8,239 — 89% silently lost, chapter 24 of 24. Six of fourteen real captures are affected. Root cause isolated by the T-0006 agent: in ArticleExtractor.bestCandidate, ancestor credit only flows up 3 levels, and the climb-to-parent step only fires when the parent's combined text stays under 3x the winning child's. Pages whose content sits in several sibling sections lose everything but the best-scoring sibling. The agent built a synthetic reproduction — 5 sibling div.chapter under body with no wrapper — that reliably collapses to 1. Note the interaction with T-0007: until original HTML is stored, every long article saved is permanently truncated with no way to repair it later. This is the strongest argument for landing T-0007 immediately.
